name: IEC three-state output qualifier
summary: Downward triangle inside an outline marking an output that can enter a high-impedance state.
description: The three-state qualifier is a small triangle pointing downwards, drawn inside the outline next to the output. It says the output has a third, high-impedance state in addition to high and low. The output is controlled by an EN input or by EN dependency.

Wherever this qualifier appears, the reader should find the controlling EN input and confirm that only one driver on the net can be enabled at once. On bus diagrams the qualifier is often shown on only the first element of an array to reduce clutter.
The qualifier does not indicate bus hold or default level when all drivers are off. A floating bus needs pull resistors or bus-keeper circuitry shown separately.
readingNotes: Find the EN input or EN dependency label that controls the output.
In arrays, the qualifier may appear only on the first element.
drawingChecklist: Place the triangle inside the outline next to the output.
Show bus defaulting components where needed.
distinction: The open-circuit diamond indicates a stage that is off in one level, not a controlled high-impedance state.
